title: Electricity & Magnetism Are One Force
hook: Move a magnet near a wire and you make electricity; run current through a wire and you make a magnet. They're two faces of the same force.
key_points: A moving electric charge creates a magnetic field — that's how electromagnets work.
A changing magnetic field drives an electric current — that's how generators work.
This two-way link unifies electricity and magnetism into electromagnetism.
Light itself is an electromagnetic wave — linked electric and magnetic fields in motion.
content_html: Electricity and magnetism look like separate phenomena, but they're deeply intertwined. In the 1800s experiments showed the connection runs both ways: a moving electric charge produces a magnetic field, and a changing magnetic field pushes electric charge into motion. Send current through a coil and it becomes a magnet; spin a magnet past a coil and you generate current.
extra_html: This two-way relationship lets us combine them into a single force, electromagnetism. It's the principle behind electric motors, generators, transformers, and the magnetic strip on a card. The unification went further still: the linked dance of electric and magnetic fields can propagate through space as a wave, and that wave is light. Radio, microwaves, visible light, and X-rays are all electromagnetic waves differing only in wavelength. Britannica recounts how the link was discovered and why it counts as one of physics' great unifications.

related.title: Electric Charge & Current
related.hook: Everything electrical comes down to charge — and an electric current is simply charge on the move.

related.title: Is Light a Wave or a Particle?
related.hook: Light behaves like a wave in some experiments and like a stream of particles in others — and the surprising answer is that it's both.

related.title: Electric and Magnetic Fields
related.hook: How does a magnet pull a paperclip it isn't touching? Through a field — an invisible region of influence that tells other charges and magnets how to feel a force.

related.title: Electromagnetic Induction: How We Make Electricity
related.hook: Almost all the electricity you use was made by waving magnets past coils of wire. A changing magnetic field pushes charge into motion — that's Faraday's great discovery.

flashcards.prompt: What happens when an electric charge moves?
flashcards.back_html: A moving charge creates a magnetic field. This is the basis of electromagnets and the deep link between electricity and magnetism.

flashcards.prompt: How does a generator produce electricity?

choices.text: A changing magnetic field drives an electric current in a wire
It creates charge out of nothing
It cools wires until current appears

flashcards.explanation_html: A changing magnetic field induces a current — the reverse of a current making a magnetic field — which is how generators work.

flashcards.prompt: According to this card, what is light?

choices.text: An electromagnetic wave — linked electric and magnetic fields in motion
A flow of electric charge through space
A purely magnetic disturbance with no electric part

flashcards.explanation_html: Electricity and magnetism are unified as electromagnetism, and light is a traveling wave of coupled electric and magnetic fields.
